_meta.rule: Keep your two-prong rule, tightened so it runs mechanically. (1) Qualify if (a) a 2025–2026 LD-2 lists one of the 8 bill numbers in its specific issues text. Match the number with a regex that ignores spacing and dots, and require the filing year to be 2025–26, because 2025 Q1 filings also list 118th-Congress S.J.Res.111–118. Or (b) a public statement, letter, action alert, ad or scorecard names the resolution, the specific sale, or 'the Joint Resolutions of Disapproval' between introduction and 30 days after the vote. Post-vote ads or praise aimed at named senators count, because they are accountability pressure. (2) Set side per bill, from a statement about that bill or the same-day pair. If none exists, side = 'unknown': report the money but assign it to no side. An LD-2 listing proves the group lobbied, not which way. J Street's filings list S.J.Res.26/33 even though it took no position on them. (3) 'Affiliated PAC' means the PAC lists the org as its connected organization on FEC Form 1, or bears the org's name. PACs linked only by shared staff are flagged 'related'. (4) Report super PAC independent expenditures separately from contributions. (5) Use the same lookback window for both sides, e.g. the senator's current six-year term. A better rule mainly fixes the side problem: today an LD-2-only org (Hadassah, FDD Action) qualifies but cannot be assigned a side.
known_gaps: LD-2 search was not exhaustive (lda.gov API was unreachable from research); more organizations may qualify.
No advocacy organization was found lobbying on the Qatar (S.J.Res. 53) or UAE (S.J.Res. 54) votes.
NORPAC, Pro-Israel America PAC and DMFI PAC are excluded because their sponsoring organizations did not qualify under the rule.
Earmarks sent to joint fundraising committees are not allocated to a senator.
United Democracy Project spends independently; its spending is shown separately and is not a contribution.
